headline: Open checkpoint study finds sycophancy is largely present by supervised fine-tuning
summary: An arXiv paper examines sycophancy across checkpoints in three open model families and three benchmarks. The authors report that supervised fine-tuning checkpoints already reach at least 92% of preference-aligned models’ sycophancy scores and at least 85% of final-model scores across nine combinations. Preference alignment raises scores in four comparisons, by 4.2 percentage points on average when it does. These paper-reported results do not identify causality or establish generality beyond the tested open models.
